title: DNA Conformational Flexibility Descriptors Improve Transcription Factor Binding Prediction Across the Protein Families
authors: Upalabdha Dey; Venkata Rajesh Yella; Aditya Kumar
one_liner_zh: 该文系统整合DNA构象柔性描述符（轴向、扭转、拉伸动态）提升跨蛋白家族的转录因子结合位点预测，结合实验与计算数据及结构机制分析，核心聚焦TF-DNA互作且方法上融合物理描述符与预测建模，高度匹配本课题。
abstract: Precise binding of transcription factors (TFs) to specific DNA sequences is fundamental to gene regulation, yet the molecular principles underpinning TF–DNA specificity remain incompletely understood. While nucleotide sequence and DNA shape are known determinants of TF binding, the role of DNA flexibility encompassing axial, torsional, and stretching dynamics— remains largely unexplored, particularly across diverse TF families. Here, we systematically integrate experimentally and computationally derived DNA flexibility descriptors into predictive models of TF–DNA binding specificity. Through extensive analyses of large-scale in vitro datasets from HT-SELEX, SELEX-Seq, protein binding microarrays encompassing mam-malian and Drosophila TFs, we demonstrate that flexibility-augmented models consistently outperform sequence based models, and DNA shape augmented models to an extent. These improvements are robust across diverse experimental platforms, and scale of the datasets, underscoring the importance of DNA conformational dynamics in indirect readout. Quantitative analyses of position-specific flexibility contributions reveal distinct “flexibility hotspots” within transcription factor binding sites and their flanking regions. This is exemplified by structural insights into the homeodomain TF MSX1, where localized DNA bendability directly correlates with enhanced binding affinity and precise recognition specificity. Finally, leveraging in vivo ChIP-Seq and DNase-Seq data from ENCODE, we further validate that DNA flexibility substantially enhances the identification of functional TF binding sites across various TF families and cellular contexts. Collectively, current findings substantiate DNA flexibility as a fundamental element of the cis -regulatory code and significantly advancing predictive frameworks of gene regulatory networks.
abstract_zh: 转录因子（TFs）对特定DNA序列的精确结合是基因调控的基础，然而支撑TF–DNA特异性的分子原理仍未完全阐明。尽管核苷酸序列和DNA形状已知是TF结合的决定因素，但涵盖轴向、扭转和拉伸动力学的DNA柔韧性作用在很大程度上仍未探索，尤其是在不同TF家族中。在此，我们系统地将实验和计算衍生的DNA柔韧性描述符整合到TF–DNA结合特异性的预测模型中。通过对来自HT-SELEX、SELEX-Seq和蛋白质结合微阵列的大规模体外数据集（涵盖哺乳动物和果蝇TFs）进行广泛分析，我们证明柔韧性增强模型始终优于基于序列的模型，并在一定程度上优于DNA形状增强模型。这些改进在多种实验平台和数据集规模上均表现稳健，凸显了DNA构象动力学在间接读取中的重要性。对位置特异性柔韧性贡献的定量分析揭示了转录因子结合位点及其侧翼区域内不同的“柔韧性热点”。这通过同源域TF MSX1的结构见解得到例证，其中局部DNA可弯曲性与增强的结合亲和力和精确的识别特异性直接相关。最后，利用ENCODE的体内ChIP-Seq和DNase-Seq数据，我们进一步验证了DNA柔韧性显著增强了跨多种TF家族和细胞环境中功能性TF结合位点的识别。总体而言，当前发现证实了DNA柔韧性作为顺式调控代码的基本要素，并显著推进了基因调控网络的预测框架。
